tree_choices.hypothesis: A combined TF-IDF representation using word n-grams and character n-grams, followed by a multinomial logistic regression classifier with explicit seed control, will capture author-specific lexical and stylistic patterns in the text feature and produce well-calibrated multiclass probabilities for EAP, HPL, and MWS.

Correct the estimator API incompatibility by instantiating LogisticRegression with solver='lbfgs' and omitting the removed multi_class keyword; scikit-learn's lbfgs path will select multinomial behavior for multiclass and allow the combined word/char TF-IDF pipeline to train.

The compatible lbfgs LogisticRegression path fixes the API failure, but the high-dimensional combined word/char TF-IDF representation likely overfits with default regularization. Using stratified internal cross-validation on train.csv to select stronger L2 regularization and feature-threshold settings should reduce variance while preserving the compatible estimator call.

Multinomial logistic-regression probabilities from a sparse TF-IDF pipeline may be poorly calibrated for log-loss despite the API-compatible estimator. Wrapping the compatible logistic regression in internal cross-validated probability calibration should better align predicted probabilities with observed author frequencies and improve negative log-loss.

The calibrated logistic model improved public-dev negative log-loss over the uncalibrated linear baseline, so the remaining error may come from applying one global regularization strength to heterogeneous word and character n-gram blocks. Internally selecting C and sublinear TF scaling by stratified cross-validation, then wrapping the final compatible LogisticRegression in the same probability-calibration procedure, should reduce under- or overfitting while retaining calibrated probabilities.

tree_choices.hypothesis: Author-identification signal on this task is dominated by lexical choice (function words, idiosyncratic vocabulary). A TF-IDF vectorizer over word 1-2 grams with sublinear_tf=True, min_df≈2, and a Multinomial LogisticRegression (lbfgs, multinomial, C tuned in {0.5,1,2,4}, class_weight balanced, seed=7) fit only on train.csv will produce well-calibrated 3-class probabilities and thus strong negative log loss.

Combining word (1-2) and char_wb (2-5) TF-IDF blocks via FeatureUnion into a single LogisticRegression (lbfgs, multinomial, C tuned, seed=7) yields lower negative log loss than either block alone because the two views encode complementary lexical and stylistic evidence that a linear model can jointly weight.

The combined word+char_wb FeatureUnion logistic regression may underperform because one shared multinomial fit and one regularization strength force word and character blocks to compete and can produce overconfident probabilities. A two-view out-of-fold stacking mechanism—separate word and char_wb logistic models, OOF probability generation, convex/meta logistic combination, and temperature/calibration fitted on OOF NLL—should learn how much to trust each view per class and correct miscalibration, improving generalization over the single joint model.

The joint word+char FeatureUnion model can be miscalibrated for negative log loss if class_weight='balanced' reweights classes and a single global C lets high-cardinality word ngrams consume the regularization budget. A mechanism of unweighted multinomial logistic regression on the FeatureUnion, with an explicit per-block scaling/mixing weight selected by internal out-of-fold negative log loss and a single temperature fit on OOF probabilities, should preserve joint-view interaction while controlling block competition and overconfidence without a learned meta-stacker.

The joint word+char_wb FeatureUnion logistic regression is the strongest completed baseline, but its probabilities may still be overconfident. A fast mechanism—fit the joint multinomial logistic regression once, then learn a single temperature scalar on a fixed stratified internal holdout and apply it to all predictions—should improve negative log loss without the expensive OOF/meta/calibration layers that caused timeout. The mechanism specifically avoids per-block weighting, per-class meta-learning, and repeated OOF fits while still correcting global overconfidence.

tree_choices.hypothesis: Standardizing the 192 numeric leaf features, reducing dimensionality with PCA to retain about 95% of variance, and fitting multinomial logistic regression on the principal components will capture the dominant class-separating variation while suppressing feature noise.

A class-balanced tree ensemble (ExtraTrees or RandomForest with class_weight balanced_subsample and many randomized trees) on the raw standardized 192 numeric features will capture nonlinear species-separating interactions and be more robust to noisy/uninformative features than the failed PCA+logistic pipeline, yielding better-calibrated multiclass probabilities for rare leaf classes.

The PCA+logistic failure likely came from unsupervised PCA discarding class-discriminative directions while retaining noisy variance and from uncalibrated linear probabilities overfitting/underfitting many rare classes. Replacing PCA with supervised feature selection on standardized features, then fitting a class-weighted L2 multinomial logistic model with nested out-of-fold probability calibration and seed averaging, should retain rare-class signal while controlling overconfidence.

The strongest observed family is the PCA plus multinomial-logistic pipeline; its main remaining risk is probability miscalibration and overconfident rare-class behavior when class weighting or calibration is added. A safer mechanism is to keep the PCA plus logistic discriminative base, estimate class priors and a temperature/shrinkage parameter by out-of-fold log-loss on the training data, and blend its calibrated probabilities with a shrunken nearest-centroid expert whose weight is also learned out-of-fold. This should correct prior and calibration drift without replacing the representation that already generalizes.

The admitted calibrated PCA+logistic plus shrunken nearest-centroid blend may still be limited by global scaling/PCA mixing the margin, shape, and texture feature blocks and by using a fixed blend/calibration weighting. A block-wise preprocessing mechanism that scales each feature group separately, reduces each block with its own PCA or denoising transform, concatenates the reduced blocks, and then fits regularized multinomial logistic regression with out-of-fold temperature/prior calibration and a cross-validated shrinkage weight for the centroid blend should preserve useful block structure and reduce overfitting to global PCA directions.

ideas.expected_observation: Predictions should have lower multiclass negative log loss than multinomial logistic regression on raw standardized features, with probabilities that remain finite and row-normalized in [0,1].
ideas.hypothesis: Standardizing the 192 numeric leaf features, reducing dimensionality with PCA to retain about 95% of variance, and fitting multinomial logistic regression on the principal components will capture the dominant class-separating variation while suppressing feature noise.

ideas.expected_observation: Validation rows should show competitive negative log loss and stable probability calibration, especially for classes with few training examples, while preserving valid probability rows.
ideas.hypothesis: A class-balanced linear model using L2-regularized multinomial logistic regression on noise-robustly scaled features will provide well-calibrated class probabilities for this many-class leaf dataset without overfitting rare species.

ideas.expected_observation: The ensemble should achieve lower negative log loss than either component alone on the mixed validation/submission rows, with all output probabilities finite, nonnegative, and summing to one per row.
ideas.hypothesis: An ensemble averaging probabilities from multinomial logistic regression and a nonlinear tree-based classifier such as RandomForest, both trained on the same scaled feature matrix, will reduce variance from any single model and improve multiclass probability quality.

ideas.hypothesis: The strongest observed family is the PCA plus multinomial-logistic pipeline; its main remaining risk is probability miscalibration and overconfident rare-class behavior when class weighting or calibration is added. A safer mechanism is to keep the PCA plus logistic discriminative base, estimate class priors and a temperature/shrinkage parameter by out-of-fold log-loss on the training data, and blend its calibrated probabilities with a shrunken nearest-centroid expert whose weight is also learned out-of-fold. ideas.expected_observation: If class weighting or supervised selection caused the collapse, unweighted regularized logistic should recover better-calibrated probabilities and improve negative log loss over the failed calibrated class-weighted variant, while keeping all rows finite and normalized.
ideas.hypothesis: The supervised-selection plus class-weighted calibrated logistic failure suggests class weighting and nested calibration may interact badly. A clean ablation should use unweighted L2 multinomial logistic regression on standardized features without aggressive supervised selection, with only out-of-fold temperature scaling and empirical-prior smoothing. This tests whether the failure came from selection instability or class weighting rather than from the linear model family itself.

ideas.expected_observation: Validation negative log loss should improve or remain competitive with the best PCA plus logistic base, with more stable probabilities across rare classes and no row-wise probability normalization failures.
ideas.hypothesis: The raw 192 features form distinct margin, shape, and texture blocks with different scales and noise properties. Standardizing globally and applying one unsupervised reduction may mix uninformative blocks with useful ones. A block-wise preprocessing mechanism that scales each feature group separately, reduces each group with its own PCA or denoising transform, concatenates the reduced blocks, and then applies regularized multinomial logistic regression with out-of-fold calibration may preserve useful group structure while controlling dimensionality and overfitting.

select.hypothesis: Standardizing the 192 numeric leaf features, reducing dimensionality with PCA to retain about 95% of variance, and fitting multinomial logistic regression on the principal components will capture the dominant class-separating variation while suppressing feature noise.

A class-balanced tree ensemble (ExtraTrees or RandomForest with class_weight balanced_subsample and many randomized trees) on the raw standardized 192 numeric features will capture nonlinear species-separating interactions and be more robust to noisy/uninformative features than the failed PCA+logistic pipeline, yielding better-calibrated multiclass probabilities for rare leaf classes.

The PCA+logistic failure likely came from unsupervised PCA discarding class-discriminative directions while retaining noisy variance and from uncalibrated linear probabilities overfitting/underfitting many rare classes. Replacing PCA with supervised feature selection on standardized features, then fitting a class-weighted L2 multinomial logistic model with nested out-of-fold probability calibration and seed averaging, should retain rare-class signal while controlling overconfidence.

The strongest observed family is the PCA plus multinomial-logistic pipeline; its main remaining risk is probability miscalibration and overconfident rare-class behavior when class weighting or calibration is added. A safer mechanism is to keep the PCA plus logistic discriminative base, estimate class priors and a temperature/shrinkage parameter by out-of-fold log-loss on the training data, and blend its calibrated probabilities with a shrunken nearest-centroid expert whose weight is also learned out-of-fold. This should correct prior and calibration drift without replacing the representation that already generalizes.

The admitted calibrated PCA+logistic plus shrunken nearest-centroid blend may still be limited by global scaling/PCA mixing the margin, shape, and texture feature blocks and by using a fixed blend/calibration weighting. A block-wise preprocessing mechanism that scales each feature group separately, reduces each block with its own PCA or denoising transform, concatenates the reduced blocks, and then fits regularized multinomial logistic regression with out-of-fold temperature/prior calibration and a cross-validated shrinkage weight for the centroid blend should preserve useful block structure and reduce overfitting to global PCA directions.

ideas.hypothesis: The strongest observed family is the PCA plus multinomial-logistic pipeline; its main remaining risk is probability miscalibration and overconfident rare-class behavior when class weighting or calibration is added. A safer mechanism is to keep the PCA plus logistic discriminative base, estimate class priors and a temperature/shrinkage parameter by out-of-fold log-loss on the training data, and blend its calibrated probabilities with a shrunken nearest-centroid expert whose weight is also learned out-of-fold. This should correct prior and calibration drift without replacing the representation that already generalizes.

ideas.expected_observation: If class weighting or supervised selection caused the collapse, unweighted regularized logistic should recover better-calibrated probabilities and improve negative log loss over the failed calibrated class-weighted variant, while keeping all rows finite and normalized.
ideas.hypothesis: The supervised-selection plus class-weighted calibrated logistic failure suggests class weighting and nested calibration may interact badly. A clean ablation should use unweighted L2 multinomial logistic regression on standardized features without aggressive supervised selection, with only out-of-fold temperature scaling and empirical-prior smoothing. This tests whether the failure came from selection instability or class weighting rather than from the linear model family itself.

ideas.expected_observation: Validation negative log loss should improve or remain competitive with the best PCA plus logistic base, with more stable probabilities across rare classes and no row-wise probability normalization failures.
ideas.hypothesis: The raw 192 features form distinct margin, shape, and texture blocks with different scales and noise properties. Standardizing globally and applying one unsupervised reduction may mix uninformative blocks with useful ones. A block-wise preprocessing mechanism that scales each feature group separately, reduces each group with its own PCA or denoising transform, concatenates the reduced blocks, and then applies regularized multinomial logistic regression with out-of-fold calibration may preserve useful group structure while controlling dimensionality and overfitting.

tree_choices.hypothesis: A standardized-feature multinomial logistic regression with L2 regularization and C selected by stratified cross-validated negative log loss will produce well-calibrated class probabilities for the 99 leaf classes and outperform unregularized or poorly scaled linear classifiers.

A class-conditional Gaussian model with shrinkage on standardized margin, shape, and texture features can capture correlated within-class feature structure and provide better-calibrated probabilities than a diagonal or standard linear model for this high-dimensional multiclass task.

The flat 99-class multinomial logistic model treats all leaf classes as exchangeable and must learn separate boundaries for many closely related species. Deriving a genus-level hierarchy from the target column names and fitting a two-stage regularized multinomial logistic model, first at genus level and then conditionally within genus for species, can share regularization and calibration across related classes; final class probabilities are normalized products of genus and within-genus species probabilities.

Because linear L2 regularization on standardized raw features may underfit nonlinear class boundaries, a low-rank kernel approximation such as Nystroem/RBF followed by strongly regularized multinomial logistic regression can model interactions among margin, shape, and texture features while preserving calibrated multiclass probabilities.

ideas.expected_observation: Lower held-out negative log loss than an unregularized multinomial logistic model, with finite probabilities in [0,1] summing to 1 per row.
ideas.hypothesis: A standardized-feature multinomial logistic regression with L2 regularization and C selected by stratified cross-validated negative log loss will produce well-calibrated class probabilities for the 99 leaf classes and outperform unregularized or poorly scaled linear classifiers.

ideas.expected_observation: Improved cross-validated negative log loss relative to an LDA or plain multinomial logistic baseline, especially if feature covariance shrinkage is tuned.
ideas.hypothesis: A class-conditional Gaussian model with shrinkage on standardized margin, shape, and texture features can capture correlated within-class feature structure and provide better-calibrated probabilities than a diagonal or standard linear model for this high-dimensional multiclass task.

ideas.expected_observation: Lower held-out negative log loss than the best single logistic or tree model, with weights favoring the logistic component when classes are numerous and features are highly collinear.

ideas.expected_observation: Better held-out negative log loss and calibration than the flat regularized multinomial alone; if centroid estimates are noisy or class distributions overlap strongly, stacking should put near-zero weight on them and not improve.
ideas.hypothesis: A fully generative class-conditional Gaussian failed, but a shrunken class-centroid similarity model using diagonal or low-rank covariance can provide stable log-probability features. select.hypothesis: A standardized-feature multinomial logistic regression with L2 regularization and C selected by stratified cross-validated negative log loss will produce well-calibrated class probabilities for the 99 leaf classes and outperform unregularized or poorly scaled linear classifiers.

A class-conditional Gaussian model with shrinkage on standardized margin, shape, and texture features can capture correlated within-class feature structure and provide better-calibrated probabilities than a diagonal or standard linear model for this high-dimensional multiclass task.

The flat 99-class multinomial logistic model treats all leaf classes as exchangeable and must learn separate boundaries for many closely related species. Deriving a genus-level hierarchy from the target column names and fitting a two-stage regularized multinomial logistic model, first at genus level and then conditionally within genus for species, can share regularization and calibration across related classes; final class probabilities are normalized products of genus and within-genus species probabilities.

Because linear L2 regularization on standardized raw features may underfit nonlinear class boundaries, a low-rank kernel approximation such as Nystroem/RBF followed by strongly regularized multinomial logistic regression can model interactions among margin, shape, and texture features while preserving calibrated multiclass probabilities.

A cross-validated block-wise supervised projection, such as PLS or Fisher/LDA directions within each block, concatenating a small number of block scores and fitting one multinomial logistic with block-specific L2 strengths, should reduce collinearity and noise while preserving class-discriminative block structure, unlike full Gaussian covariance or noisy genus hierarchy.

ideas.expected_observation: Improved held-out negative log loss over raw flat logistic when block nonlinearities are present; excessive random features or weak regularization should degrade calibration.
ideas.hypothesis: The flat multinomial may underfit nonlinear interactions among the margin, shape, and texture features. Computing separate random Fourier or RBF feature maps for each feature block, then fitting a single L2-regularized multinomial logistic regression on the concatenated block maps, can model block-specific nonlinear class boundaries with controlled variance while avoiding a full 192-dimensional kernel expansion.

ideas.expected_observation: Better held-out negative log loss and calibration than the flat regularized multinomial alone; if centroid estimates are noisy or class distributions overlap strongly, stacking should put near-zero weight on them and not improve.
ideas.hypothesis: A fully generative class-conditional Gaussian failed, but a shrunken class-centroid similarity model using diagonal or low-rank covariance can provide stable log-probability features. Stacking these centroid log-probabilities with the flat regularized multinomial logits, with stacking weights chosen by cross-validation, can recover compact-cluster structure that linear logistic underweights while avoiding unstable full covariance estimation.
